messages:
jordan (Acme): Hey, we started noticing gaps in our SIEM events around 2026-03-16 02:00 UTC. Splunk shows a bunch of older timestamps arriving after newer ones. Some alerts didn't trigger.
anna (Support): Sorry to hear that — can you confirm tenant id and any export name? Also, did you see any 403s or decryption errors in the manifest consumer?
jordan (Acme): Tenant: acme-inc, export: audit-export-prod-us. No 403s in Splunk, just events with older event_time fields than expected. We also saw a few zero-byte blobs in the manifest payload.
miguel (SRE): tagging @sara. Quick checks: are manifests being re-ordered in S3 (manifest file timestamps vs objects)? Can you paste the manifest key(s)?
jordan (Acme): example manifest: s3://exports/acme-inc/audit/2026/03/16/02/manifest-20260316020000.json
jordan (Acme): attached (pasted) — many object entries show upload_time 2026-03-16T02:05:xxZ but event_time 2026-03-16T01:50:xxZ
sara (Security): Could be due to late-arriving events that were backfilled, or a replay step. Any KMS/ECDSA/ HSM errors in the forwarder logs? We had a key rotation window at ~02:03 UTC earlier.
anna (Support): Can you run this from your side to list manifests and object timestamps? ```aws s3 ls s3://exports/acme-inc/audit/2026/03/16/02/ --recursive | sort``` 
jordan (Acme): ran it, results show objects uploaded at 02:05-02:07 but manifest timestamp is 02:02. There are also a few zero-byte objects: `.../chunk-xyz.gz 0`.
miguel (SRE): zero-byte objects indicate a producer failure in the uploader. @ingest-eng can you check the manifest builder/lifecycle? Might be a race where manifest written before all parts uploaded.
ingest-eng: Looking at the upload pipeline: we had a transient S3 500 at 02:04 causing retries; manifest writer didn't wait for all successful puts. Reproducer: induce S3 500 between chunk upload and manifest finalize. Fix: add final listing + confirm checksums before manifest commit. PR queued.
sara (Security): Also, KMS rotation — we rotated alias `alias/audit-export` at 02:03 but HSM ops reported a held-back operation for ~90s. It's possible some records were re-encrypted with the new key after initial manifest produced (causing event_time reorder). Need to ensure atomicity of encryption+manifest.
miguel (SRE): Action items: 1) Support to orchestrate replay for affected window 02:00-02:10, 2) Ingest to patch manifest writer with final listing, 3) Security to confirm KMS rotation telemetry and whether any decrypt failures were logged.
anna (Support): Jordan — we'll enqueue a replay job now for acme-inc 2026-03-16T02:00:00Z -> 2026-03-16T02:10:00Z and prioritize delivery to Splunk. ETA ~30m. Will follow up with ticket link.
jordan (Acme): thanks. Please include any forensic logs — Splunk team needs to reconcile alerts.
ops-bot: replay job created: job_id=rb-20260316-2523456789-01 status=queued
miguel (SRE): Repro steps we used in staging to simulate: 1) throttled S3 PUTs for 10s, 2) force manifest commit early, 3) re-encrypt chunk with new KMS key; observe out-of-order event_time in manifest consumer. Snippet: ```# simulate S3 failure tc qdisc add dev eth0 root netem loss 30%``` 
sara (Security): For the replay, we should also ensure re-encryption uses correct key id and publish a note about the rotation window to customers (apology + mitigation).
anna (Support): Ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/EXP-4123 — I've added logs and the manifest sample. Assigning to @miguel and @ingest-eng. We'll post status updates here. :white_check_mark:
jordan (Acme): appreciate the quick response. I'll pause any local dedup logic until replay finishes.
miguel (SRE): follow-up: ingest patch merged to canary at 02:40 UTC; replay run started 02:44 UTC. Initial delivery to Splunk shows events now ordered; no decrypt errors observed during replay. Closing provisional.
anna (Support): Closing once ACME confirms all missing alerts reconciled. Jordan, can you confirm?
jordan (Acme): Confirmed — Splunk shows the backfilled events and alerts re-fired where expected. Thanks everyone. :tada:
